q: Which of the following commissions/committees identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
solution:
The correct answer is Justice Verma Committee.

Key Points

• The Justice Verma Committee was established to recommend amendments to criminal laws to provide for quicker trial and enhanced punishment for criminals accused of committing sexual assault against women.

• One of the significant contributions of the Justice Verma Committee was identifying the existence of legal provisions for the implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties.

• The Committee underscored the importance of fundamental duties as a counterpart to fundamental rights, emphasizing their role in ensuring the proper functioning of democracy.

• The recommendations of the Justice Verma Committee have been instrumental in shaping reforms in India's legal framework, especially concerning women's safety and legal provisions related to fundamental duties.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties:

• Fundamental Duties are specified in Part IV-A of the Indian Constitution (Article 51A).

• They were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• Originally, ten duties were listed; the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, added an eleventh duty.

• These duties are moral obligations on all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and to uphold the unity of India.

• Justice Verma Committee:

• The Justice Verma Committee was constituted in the wake of the 2012 Delhi gang-rape case.

• It was tasked with reviewing existing laws and suggesting changes to ensure the safety and dignity of women.

• Its report, submitted in January 2013, made several landmark recommendations for legal reforms.

• The Committee's work led to the enactment of the Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013, which introduced stricter penalties for sexual crimes.

• Sarkaria Commission:

• Formed in 1983, the Sarkaria Commission was set up to review the working of the Indian federal system and the balance of power between the state and central governments.

• It submitted its report in 1988 with recommendations to improve center-state relations.

• Rajamannar Commission:

• The Rajamannar Committee, established by the Tamil Nadu government in 1969, was tasked with examining center-state relations.

• It recommended greater autonomy for states and the establishment of a permanent inter-state council.

q: Agricultural shot is a term used in which of the following sports?
solution:
The correct answer is Cricket.

Key Points

• The term "Agricultural shot" is used in Cricket to describe an unorthodox or poorly executed shot.

• In cricket, an agricultural shot typically refers to a wild swing of the bat, which is not played with the standard technique.

• This type of shot often results in the ball going in an unintended direction, usually not as per the plan of the batsman.

• It is generally considered to be a high-risk shot, often played in desperation or by less technically skilled players.

Additional Information

• Cricket Terminologies:

• Cover Drive: A classic cricket shot played by driving the ball through the covers with a vertical bat.

• Yorker: A delivery bowled right at the batsman's feet, typically aimed at the base of the stumps.

• Duckworth-Lewis Method: A complex mathematical formula used to calculate the target score for the team batting second in a limited-overs cricket match interrupted by weather or other circumstances.

• Leg Spin: A type of spin bowling where the ball spins from the leg side to the off side (for a right-handed batsman).

• All-rounder: A player who excels at both batting and bowling.

• Types of Shots in Cricket:

• Straight Drive: A shot played straight down the ground with a vertical bat.

• Sweep: A shot played to a ball pitched on or outside the leg stump, typically hit towards the leg side.

• Pull Shot: A cross-batted shot played to a short-pitched ball, usually hit towards the leg side.

• Cut Shot: A shot played to a ball pitched short and wide of off stump, hit towards the point or gully region.

• Hook Shot: A shot played to a bouncer, where the batsman hits the ball towards the leg side, typically into the stands.

• Cricket Fielding Positions:

• Slip: A fielding position behind the batsman on the off side, typically placed to catch edges from the bat.

• Gully: Positioned between the slips and point, intended to catch edges that slip through.

• Mid-wicket: A position on the leg side, in the region square of the wicket.

• Long-on: Positioned straight down the ground, typically near the boundary.

• Square Leg: A position on the leg side, square with the wicket.

q: In chess, which of the following may only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it?
solution:
The correct answer is The Pawn.

Key Points

• A pawn can only move forward to the unoccupied square immediately in front of it on the same file.

• On its first move, a pawn has the option to move forward two squares.

• Pawns capture diagonally, one square forward and to the left or right.

• If a pawn reaches the opposite end of the board, it can be promoted to any other piece, typically a queen.

Additional Information

• Chess Pieces and Their Movements:

• The Bishop: The bishop moves diagonally any number of squares. Each bishop starts on one color (light or dark) and must always stay on that color.

• The Queen: The queen can move any number of squares along a rank, file, or diagonal. It is the most powerful piece in terms of mobility.

• The Rook: The rook can move any number of squares along a rank or file. Rooks also play a crucial role in the endgame due to their ability to control large portions of the board.

• The Knight: The knight moves in an "L" shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular. Knights are unique because they can "jump" over other pieces.

• The King: The king moves one square in any direction. The objective of the game is to checkmate the opponent's king.

• Special Pawn Moves:

• En Passant: This special pawn capture can occur if a pawn moves two squares forward from its starting position and lands beside an opponent's pawn. The opponent's pawn can capture it "en passant" (in passing), as if it had only moved one square.

q: Which Committee identified the existence of legal provisions for implementation of some of the Fundamental Duties?
solution:
The correct answer is Justice Verma Committee.

• The Committee was set up in 1999 under the chairmanship of Justice J.S. Verma, former Chief Justice of India.

• It reviewed the existing legal framework and suggested measures to make the Fundamental Duties more enforceable.

• The Committee's recommendations emphasized the role of education and awareness in promoting a sense of duty among citizens.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties

• The Fundamental Duties are a set of moral obligations for all citizens of India, enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution (Article 51A).

• These duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.

• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, which include respect for the Constitution, national symbols, the promotion of harmony, and the protection of public property.

• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts.

• Justice Verma Committee

• Justice J.S. Verma, a renowned jurist and former Chief Justice of India, chaired the committee.

• The Committee's focus was to enhance the implementation of Fundamental Duties through legal and educational reforms.

• It highlighted the need for incorporating the Fundamental Duties into the education system to instill a sense of responsibility in citizens from a young age.

• The Committee's report has been influential in shaping policies and programs aimed at promoting civic responsibility.

• 42nd Amendment Act, 1976

• The 42nd Amendment Act is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its extensive changes to the Constitution of India.

• It introduced the Fundamental Duties, provided for the establishment of Administrative Tribunals, and made several changes to the Preamble and other parts of the Constitution.

• The Amendment was passed during the Emergency period under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government.

• It aimed to strengthen the central government's powers and bring about socio-economic reforms.

q: The term Blue Line is associated with which of the following games?
solution:
The correct answer is Ice Hockey.

Key Points

• The term "Blue Line" is a significant part of the game Ice Hockey.

• It refers to the lines that divide the hockey rink into three zones: the defending zone, neutral zone, and attacking zone.

• The blue lines play a crucial role in determining offside violations in the game of ice hockey.

• They are essential in regulating the flow of the game and ensuring that players adhere to the rules related to positioning on the rink.

Additional Information

• Offside Rule in Ice Hockey

• The offside rule is one of the fundamental rules in ice hockey, aimed at preventing players from gaining an unfair advantage.

• A player is considered offside if they enter the attacking zone before the puck crosses the blue line.

• If an offside violation occurs, the referee stops the play, and a faceoff is conducted in the neutral zone to resume the game.

• Understanding the offside rule is crucial for players and coaches as it impacts offensive strategies and game planning.

• Zones on the Rink

• The ice hockey rink is divided into three zones by two blue lines: the defending zone, the neutral zone, and the attacking zone.

• The defending zone is the area between the blue line closest to a team's goal and the end boards.

• The neutral zone lies between the two blue lines, where much of the game's transition play occurs.

• The attacking zone is the area between the blue line farthest from a team's goal and the end boards, where a team aims to score goals.

• Importance of the Blue Line

• The blue lines are critical for maintaining the structure and flow of the game, ensuring that players adhere to the rules of positioning.

• They are used to judge offside violations and play a role in determining where faceoffs occur on the rink.

• Blue lines also contribute to the strategic aspects of the game, influencing how teams execute their offensive and defensive plays.

• Properly understanding and leveraging the blue lines can provide a competitive edge to teams in ice hockey.

q: In chess which of the following may move only diagonally?
solution:
The correct answer is The Bishop.

Key Points

• The Bishop is a piece in the game of chess that can move diagonally on the board.

• Each player starts the game with two Bishops, placed on either side of the King and Queen.

• The Bishop can move any number of squares along the diagonal, but cannot jump over other pieces.

• The Bishop's movement allows it to control squares of only one color throughout the game.

Additional Information

• Chess Pieces and Their Movements:

• The Knight: Moves in an L-shape: two squares in one direction and then one square perpendicular to that direction. It is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.

• The Queen: Can move any number of squares along a row, column, or diagonal. It combines the power of the Rook and Bishop.

• The Rook: Moves any number of squares along a row or column but cannot move diagonally.

• The Pawn: Moves forward one square, but captures diagonally. On its first move, it can move forward two squares.

• The King: Moves one square in any direction. The objective of the game is to checkmate the opponent's King.

• Chessboard Layout:

• The chessboard is an 8x8 grid with alternating light and dark squares.

• Each player begins with 16 pieces: one King, one Queen, two Rooks, two Knights, two Bishops, and eight Pawns.

• The pieces are placed on the two rows closest to each player, with Pawns on the second row and the major pieces on the first row.

• Objective of the Game:

• The primary objective in chess is to checkmate the opponent's King, which means the King is in a position to be captured (in check) and there is no legal move to escape.

• Players must use strategy and tactics to outmaneuver their opponent and gain a positional or material advantage.

q: 'Castling' is related to which of the following sports?
solution:
The correct answer is Chess.

Key Points

• Castling is a unique move in chess involving the king and one of the rooks.

• It is the only move in chess where two pieces, the king and a rook, move simultaneously.

• Castling can only be done if neither the king nor the rook involved has previously moved, and there are no pieces between them.

• The purpose of castling is often to protect the king and to develop the rook.

Additional Information

• Castling Conditions:

• Neither the king nor the rook involved in castling may have previously moved.

• There must be no pieces between the king and the rook.

• The squares the king passes over must not be under attack.

• The king may not be in check before or after castling.

• Types of Castling:

• There are two types of castling: kingside (short) and queenside (long).

• In kingside castling, the king moves two squares towards the kingside rook and the rook moves to the square next to the king.

• In queenside castling, the king moves two squares towards the queenside rook and the rook moves to the square next to the king.

• Strategic Importance:

• Castling is a key strategic move that helps in the protection of the king by placing it behind a wall of pawns.

• It also helps in bringing the rook into play, connecting the rooks, and developing the pieces for the middle game.

q: Why is the weight and circumference of a cricket ball strictly regulated in official matches?
options: Heavier balls suit bowlers, lighter ones suit batsmen, so balance is needed
Variations affect bounce, swing, and fairness on standard pitches
ICC mandates it to cut costs and simplify logistics
Only red balls follow this; white balls have separate norms
solution:
The correct answer is Variations affect bounce, swing, and fairness on standard pitches.

Key Points

• Regulation by ICC: The International Cricket Council (ICC) strictly regulates the weight and circumference of cricket balls in official matches to maintain uniformity and fairness across all formats of the game.

• Impact on performance: Variations in weight and size significantly affect the bounce, swing, and spin of the ball. These factors are crucial in determining the outcome of matches and ensuring equal opportunities for both bowlers and batsmen.

• Standard pitches: Standard pitches are designed with specific dimensions and characteristics. Cricket balls must conform to regulated specifications to ensure predictable behavior on these pitches, contributing to a balanced contest.

• Consistency in gameplay: Uniformity in ball specifications helps ensure consistency in gameplay across different venues and conditions, fostering fair competition.

• Quality assurance: Strict regulations ensure that cricket balls are produced with high-quality materials and standardized manufacturing processes, preventing any unfair advantages or discrepancies.

Additional Information

• Specifications for Cricket Balls:

• The weight of a cricket ball must be between 156 grams and 163 grams as per ICC regulations.

• The circumference should be between 22.4 cm and 22.9 cm.

• Red balls are used in Test matches, while white balls are used in ODIs and T20s.

• Different ball brands such as Kookaburra, Dukes, and SG are used globally, with slight variations in seam and finish.

• Impact of Ball Variations:

• Heavier balls may offer more swing, while lighter balls might favor batsmen due to less movement.

• The seam plays a critical role in generating spin and swing, affecting bowler performance.

• Changes in ball dimensions can disrupt the balance between batting and bowling, leading to unfair outcomes.

• Role of ICC in Cricket:

• The ICC is the governing body for international cricket, responsible for standardizing rules, regulations, and equipment specifications.

• Its guidelines ensure uniformity in gameplay across various formats and tournaments.

• ICC also monitors ball manufacturing to uphold these standards.

• Red vs. White Balls:

• Red balls: Used in longer formats, they have a pronounced seam for better swing and spin.

• White balls: Used in limited-overs formats, they are treated for durability under floodlights.

• White balls tend to deteriorate faster, affecting their performance over time.

Important Points

• Advantages of Standardized Cricket Balls:

• Ensures fair gameplay and equal opportunities for all players.

• Maintains consistency across matches played in different regions and conditions.

• Helps bowlers and batsmen strategize effectively based on predictable ball behavior.

• Examples of ICC Regulations:

• In Test cricket, only red balls conforming to ICC specifications are permitted.

• In ODIs and T20s, white balls are used, but they must meet the same weight and circumference standards as red balls.

• Special cases like pink balls are used for day-night Test matches but are also regulated for consistency.

q: Which of the following commissions recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre-State cooperation?
solution:
The correct answer is Sarkaria Commission.

Key Points

• The Sarkaria Commission was established by the Government of India in June 1983 to review the Centre-State relations.

• It recommended the establishment of a Permanent Secretariat for the Inter-State Council to institutionalize Centre-State cooperation.

• The Inter-State Council is a constitutional body under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and States.

• The Sarkaria Commission emphasized the need for better communication and coordination between the Centre and States to strengthen federalism in India.

• Its recommendations led to the formation of the Inter-State Council in 1990, which serves as an important platform for resolving disputes and promoting cooperative federalism.

Additional Information

• Rajamannar Committee

• It was set up by the Tamil Nadu government in 1969 under the chairmanship of P.V. Rajamannar.

• The committee recommended more autonomy to states and a redefinition of Centre-State relations.

• It suggested the abolition of the Planning Commission, the discontinuation of All India Services, and the transfer of subjects from the Union List to the State List.

• However, its recommendations were not implemented at the national level.

• Punchhi Commission

• The Punchhi Commission was set up in April 2007 under the chairmanship of Justice M.M. Punchhi to look into Centre-State relations.

• It recommended a fixed term for Governors, a comprehensive framework for disaster management, and changes to the role of the Governor in state politics.

• It focused on addressing challenges to federalism in the context of globalization and socio-economic changes.

• Its report is considered significant for improving Centre-State relations but is yet to be fully implemented.

• Venkatachelliah Commission

• Also known as the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution (NCRWC), it was established in 2000 under Justice M.N. Venkatachaliah.

• The commission aimed to review the Constitution to make it more effective and relevant in contemporary times.

• It suggested reforms in electoral processes, judicial accountability, and the functioning of parliamentary institutions.

• It did not specifically focus on Centre-State relations or the Inter-State Council.

q: Which of the following statements about cricket dismissals is correct?
options: Hitting the ball twice deliberately results in dismissal.
Retired Out' requires only umpire approval.
Obstructing the Field' can occur accidentally.
Retired Out' happens automatically without any approval.
solution:
The correct answer is Hitting the ball twice deliberately results in dismissal..

Key Points

• Hitting the ball twice deliberately is considered an illegal action in cricket and results in dismissal under the laws of the game.

• This dismissal is covered under Law 34 of the MCC Laws of Cricket, which prohibits a batter from intentionally striking the ball twice unless it is done to defend their wicket.

• Such an action is judged by the umpire, who determines whether the batter deliberately hit the ball twice.

• The first strike is considered legitimate (e.g., hitting the ball with the bat), but the second strike intended to gain runs or mislead the fielding team constitutes a breach.

• This rule upholds the integrity of fair play in cricket and ensures that the batter does not use unfair methods to gain an advantage.

Additional Information

• Retired Out:

• A player retiring out does not need umpire approval; it is the batter's voluntary decision.

• Unlike "retired hurt," where a player leaves due to injury with an option to return, "retired out" is final and does not allow re-entry into the game.

• This form of dismissal is uncommon and usually occurs in practice matches or under special circumstances.

• Obstructing the Field:

• According to Law 37 of the MCC Laws of Cricket, "Obstructing the Field" occurs when a batter deliberately interferes with a fielder attempting to field or catch the ball.

• This dismissal is not accidental; it requires clear intent by the batter to obstruct the fielding side.

• Examples include using the bat or body to stop the ball while a fielder is attempting to effect a run-out or catch.

• Accidental interference, such as running in the path of a fielder without intent, does not constitute this dismissal.

• Cricket Dismissals:

• There are several ways a batter can be dismissed in cricket, including bowled, caught, leg before wicket (LBW), stumped, and run-out.

• Other less common dismissals include obstructing the field, retired out, hitting the ball twice, and timed out.

• Each type of dismissal has specific rules outlined by the MCC Laws of Cricket and is subject to umpire judgment.

q: In freestyle wrestling, which of the following actions can result in a technical point for the wrestler?

• Grabbing the opponent's singlet, headgear, or other parts of their uniform is prohibited in freestyle wrestling.

• This action is considered illegal and results in penalties or warnings against the wrestler committing the foul.

• The purpose of this rule is to ensure fairness and maintain the integrity of the sport.

• An illegal headlock occurs when a wrestler applies a headlock without an arm included in the hold.

• This technique is not allowed as it can cause serious injuries and is against the rules of freestyle wrestling.

• Wrestlers using illegal holds may face penalties, warnings, or even disqualification in extreme cases.

• This refers to when a team wins two matches in a row, showcasing consistency and strong performance over multiple games.

q: Which of the following is true about "en passant" in chess?
options: Only after a pawn moves two squares and waits a turn.
Can be done within two moves after the pawn's advance.
Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.
Only if the capturing pawn is on a dark square.
solution:
The correct answer is Must be done immediately after the pawn moves two squares.

Key Points

• En passant is a special pawn capture rule in chess that allows a pawn to capture an opponent's pawn immediately after it moves two squares forward from its starting position.

• The capture must be made on the very next move; otherwise, the opportunity is lost.

• The opponent's pawn must have moved two squares forward from its starting position, landing adjacent to the capturing pawn.

• When the en passant capture occurs, the capturing pawn moves diagonally to the square where the opponent's pawn would have landed if it had advanced only one square.

• The rule was introduced to prevent pawns from bypassing a potential capture when advancing two squares, maintaining fairness in the game.

Additional Information

• Pieces & Board

• Pieces: King, Queen, Rook, Bishop, Knight, Pawn.

• Board: Chessboard, Center (e4, d4, e5, d5), Ranks (rows), Files (columns).

• Game States & Results

• Check: King is attacked.

• Checkmate: King is attacked and cannot escape (Game Over).

• Stalemate: No legal moves, but not in check (Draw).

• Draw: Tie game (e.g., Perpetual Check, Threefold Repetition).

q:
Arrange the following in chronological order:

A) Sarkaria Commission report submitted

B) Inter-State Council constituted

C) Punchhi Commission constituted
solution:
The correct answer is A-B-C.

Key Points

• Sarkaria Commission: The Sarkaria Commission, constituted in 1983, submitted its report in 1988. It was formed to examine the relationship and balance of power between the central and state governments in India.

• Inter-State Council: Based on the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission, the Inter-State Council was constituted in 1990 under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution. It aims to foster cooperation and coordination between the center and the states.

• Punchhi Commission: The Punchhi Commission was constituted in 2007 to review the working of the center-state relations, and it submitted its report in 2010.

• The chronological order of events is: Sarkaria Commission report submission (1988) → Inter-State Council constitution (1990) → Punchhi Commission constitution (2007).

• The correct sequence ensures a logical progression of events based on the timeline of their occurrence.

Additional Information

• Sarkaria Commission:

• Set up in June 1983 by the Government of India under Justice R.S. Sarkaria.

• Its primary focus was on examining and recommending changes to strengthen center-state relations in the Indian federal structure.

• The report emphasized cooperative federalism and made several recommendations, including the establishment of the Inter-State Council.

• It highlighted the importance of decentralization and the active role of states in national governance.

• Inter-State Council:

• Constituted in 1990 under Article 263 of the Indian Constitution.

• Aims to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the center and the states or among the states themselves.

• Plays a significant role in promoting cooperative federalism and resolving inter-state disputes.

• Chaired by the Prime Minister and includes members from both the central and state governments.

• Punchhi Commission:

• Established in 2007 under the chairmanship of Justice M.M. Punchhi.

• Its mandate was to examine and review the working of existing arrangements between the center and the states.

• The commission submitted its report in 2010, consisting of recommendations on various issues, including emergency provisions, center-state financial relations, and better mechanisms for dispute resolution.

• One key recommendation was to include a provision for a "cooperative federalism framework" in the Constitution.

• Theme of the Question:

• The question revolves around the evolution of center-state relations in India and the initiatives taken to strengthen cooperative federalism.

• The Sarkaria and Punchhi Commissions, along with the Inter-State Council, are key milestones in this context, aiming to promote effective governance and coordination between various levels of government.

q: What is the standard width of a singles badminton court as per international regulations?

• The court is divided by a net at the center, with a height of 1.55 meters at the edges and 1.524 meters in the center.

• The sidelines for singles matches are marked inward from the outermost boundary, reducing the width from 6.10 meters (doubles width) to 5.18 meters.

• These regulations are consistent worldwide and are strictly followed in all international competitions.

• The court length is equally divided by the net, creating two halves of 6.70 meters each.

• This dimension ensures uniformity in competitive play across all levels.

• Option 4: 12.00 meters

• 12.00 meters is not a standard measurement in badminton court dimensions as per BWF regulations.

• The correct length of a badminton court is 13.40 meters, with no dimension reduced to 12.00 meters in any format of the game.

q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding the Golden Raid and card system in Kabaddi?
options: A team is allowed two Golden Raids before the result is decided.
A Green Card leads to a 2-minute suspension from the game.
A fresh toss is taken if the match is tied even after 5-5 raids.
A Red Card results in a warning with no match suspension.
solution:
The correct answer is A fresh toss is taken if the match is tied even after 5-5 raids.

Key Points

• In Kabaddi, if the match remains tied even after five raids by each team in the Golden Raid phase, a fresh toss is conducted to determine the next course of action.

• This rule ensures a fair opportunity for both teams and avoids indefinite extensions of the match duration.

• The Golden Raid is a tiebreaker mechanism where each team gets five raids to score points and secure a win.

• In the event of another tie after the Golden Raid phase, the fresh toss decides which team gets to initiate the next set of raids.

• This format introduces an element of strategy and luck, as the toss winner gains a tactical advantage by choosing to raid or defend first.

Additional Information

• Option 1: A team is allowed two Golden Raids before the result is decided

• This statement is incorrect. In Kabaddi, the Golden Raid phase involves only one set of five raids per team.

• The Golden Raid rule is designed to prevent excessive delays in determining the winner and ensures that the game concludes efficiently.

• Option 2: A Green Card leads to a 2-minute suspension from the game

• This statement is incorrect as well. A Green Card in Kabaddi serves as a warning to players or coaches for misconduct or minor rule violations.

• It does not result in any suspension or time penalty; however, repeated warnings can escalate to Yellow or Red Cards.

• Option 4: A Red Card results in a warning with no match suspension

• This statement is also incorrect. A Red Card in Kabaddi signifies a serious offense and leads to the immediate suspension of the player for the remainder of the match.

q: The "Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project" links India with which country?
solution:
The correct answer is Myanmar.

Key Points

• The Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project is an important initiative by the Government of India to connect the northeastern region of India with Myanmar through a multimodal transport network.

• It involves a combination of shipping, inland water, and road transport to provide an alternative route for trade and connectivity.

• The project spans from the port of Kolkata to the Sittwe port in Myanmar via the Bay of Bengal, followed by inland water transport on the Kaladan River up to Paletwa in Myanmar, and further by road to Mizoram in India.

• The Kaladan project aims to enhance bilateral trade between India and Myanmar and improve connectivity to the landlocked northeastern states of India, reducing dependence on the Siliguri Corridor (also known as the Chicken's Neck).

• The development of this project is expected to strengthen India’s Act East Policy by improving economic and strategic ties with Southeast Asian countries.

Additional Information

• China

• China shares borders with northeastern India, but no direct bilateral project like the Kaladan is in place between the two nations for enhancing connectivity to northeastern states.

• China is an important regional player in South Asia and Southeast Asia, but its Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) is a separate global infrastructure project that does not directly involve the Kaladan project.

• Bangladesh

• India and Bangladesh have several connectivity projects, such as the Maitri Setu and the Agartala-Akhaura rail link, but they are separate from the Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project.

• Bangladesh is a critical partner for India in terms of regional connectivity, especially for the northeastern states, under various bilateral and regional initiatives like the BBIN (Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal) framework.

• Nepal

• Nepal is a landlocked country that shares borders with India but is not part of the Kaladan project.

• India and Nepal have separate bilateral agreements for trade and transit, such as access to Indian ports for Nepalese trade.

• Main Theme: Kaladan Multimodal Transit Transport Project

• The project is part of India’s effort to establish seamless connectivity with Southeast Asia and strengthen its strategic and economic ties in the region.

• It also aims to provide an alternative route for the transportation of goods to the northeast, bypassing the narrow and congested Siliguri Corridor.

• Once completed, the project is expected to significantly reduce transportation costs and time for goods moving between India and Myanmar.

q: In the 2025 Global Firepower (GFP) review, which of the following statements is correct regarding the ranking methodology?
options: It considers only the number of active military personnel
It ranks nations solely based on nuclear capabilities
It uses over 60 factors including logistics and geography to calculate the PowerIndex
It ranks countries alphabetically within continents
solution:
The correct answer is It uses over 60 factors including logistics and geography to calculate the PowerIndex.

Key Points

• The Global Firepower (GFP) review is an annual military strength ranking that evaluates nations based on their military capabilities.

• The PowerIndex (PwrIndx) score is calculated using over 60 individual factors, encompassing categories like manpower, equipment, natural resources, financial stability, and geography.

• The ranking methodology emphasizes diversity over quantity; for instance, having a balanced mix of naval assets is more favorable than having a large fleet of a single type.

• Geography plays a crucial role, as nations with strategic locations or extensive coastlines may gain an advantage in specific areas.

• Nuclear stockpiles are considered but do not dominate the ranking system, ensuring non-nuclear nations can also rank competitively.

Additional Information

• Option 1: It considers only the number of active military personnel

• This statement is incorrect because the GFP ranking is not solely based on manpower but evaluates a comprehensive range of factors.

• While active military personnel is an important component, other elements like reserve forces, equipment, and logistics are equally significant.

• Focusing only on manpower would ignore critical aspects like training, technology, and operational readiness.

• Option 2: It ranks nations solely based on nuclear capabilities

• This is incorrect as nuclear capability is only one of the factors considered in the GFP ranking.

• The review includes nuclear stockpiles but ensures that non-nuclear powers are not unfairly disadvantaged.

• The methodology focuses on overall military potential rather than singular factors like nuclear weapons.

• Option 4: It ranks countries alphabetically within continents

• This option is incorrect as the GFP ranking is based on calculated PowerIndex scores and not alphabetical or regional order.

• Countries are ranked globally, with their position determined by overall military strength rather than their location or name.

• Global Firepower (GFP) Overview

• The GFP review is widely recognized for its thorough and unbiased assessment of military strength.

• The ranking includes data from 145 nations, providing a comprehensive analysis of global military power.

• The PowerIndex score is inversely proportional, meaning a lower score indicates a stronger and more capable military.

• It excludes political or current conflict considerations, focusing purely on measurable military factors.

q: Which of the following statements about Judo techniques and rules is correct?
options: Shime-Waza are arm locks targeting the elbows.
A Judo match ends immediately if a player scores an Ippon or receives a Hansoku-make.
Judoka can strike and kick but cannot attack joints other than elbows.
Hansoku-make is a minor penalty in Judo.
solution:
The correct answer is option 2.

Key Points

• In Judo, a match ends immediately if a player scores an Ippon, which is equivalent to a full point, or receives a Hansoku-make, which signifies disqualification.

• Ippon is awarded when a player executes a perfect technique, such as a throw where the opponent lands on their back with force and control, or achieves a successful pin for 20 seconds.

• Hansoku-make refers to a serious violation of Judo rules, such as prohibited actions or dangerous techniques, which results in the immediate disqualification of the player.

• This rule ensures safety and adherence to the principles of Judo, emphasizing respect, discipline, and fair play during the match.

• The immediate termination of the match upon Ippon or Hansoku-make is a fundamental aspect of Judo competitions and aligns with the sport’s emphasis on decisive outcomes.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Shime-Waza are arm locks targeting the elbows

• This statement is incorrect. Shime-Waza refers to choking techniques in Judo, which involve restricting the opponent’s airflow or blood flow to induce submission.

• The arm locks targeting the elbows in Judo are categorized under Kansetsu-Waza, not Shime-Waza.

• Kansetsu-Waza techniques are designed to apply pressure on joints, particularly the elbows, forcing the opponent to submit.

• Option 3: Judoka can strike and kick but cannot attack joints other than elbows

• This statement is incorrect. Strikes and kicks are strictly prohibited in Judo as it is a grappling martial art focused on throws, pins, joint locks, and chokeholds.

• Judoka are allowed to attack joints only within the scope of Kansetsu-Waza, and even then, only the elbow joint is targeted.

• The prohibition of strikes and kicks reflects Judo’s emphasis on technique, control, and safety rather than brute force or aggression.

• Option 4: Hansoku-make is a minor penalty in Judo

• This statement is incorrect. Hansoku-make is not a minor penalty; it is the most severe penalty in Judo and leads to immediate disqualification.

• Minor penalties in Judo are referred to as Shido, which are warnings for less severe rule violations, such as passivity or improper gripping.

• Hansoku-make is awarded for major rule violations, such as dangerous techniques, unsportsmanlike behavior, or repeated minor penalties.

• Main Theme: Judo Techniques and Rules

• Judo is a modern martial art and Olympic sport developed by Jigoro Kano in Japan. It focuses on techniques such as throws (Nage-Waza), ground techniques (Ne-Waza), pins (Osaekomi-Waza), joint locks (Kansetsu-Waza), and chokes (Shime-Waza).

• The rules of Judo are designed to ensure fairness and safety, with penalties for violations and clear criteria for scoring.

• The emphasis is on skill, precision, and the use of an opponent’s energy and movement to execute techniques effectively.

q: What is the standard length of the zone where runners exchange the baton in a relay race?
solution:
The correct answer is 20 meters.

• The standard length of the baton exchange zone is 20 meters, as per regulations established by the International Association of Athletics Federations (IAAF).

• The exchange zone starts 10 meters before and ends 10 meters after the designated start point of the next runner's leg in the relay.

• The proper exchange of the baton within this 20-meter zone is critical; any exchange outside the zone results in disqualification.

• The rules are designed to ensure fairness and maintain the integrity of the competition, as well as to avoid accidents during the exchange process.

Additional Information

• 10 meters:

• 10 meters is the length of the "acceleration zone" provided to the incoming runner before they enter the baton exchange zone.

• It is a preparatory area in which the next runner can build momentum before receiving the baton.

• However, the baton must still be passed within the 20-meter exchange zone, not the acceleration zone.

• 15 meters:

• There is no official rule in athletics that specifies a 15-meter exchange zone.

• This option is incorrect and does not align with IAAF regulations for relay races.

• 30 meters:

• 30 meters is not associated with the baton exchange zone in relay races.

• This length is much longer than the standardized exchange zone, which is strictly set at 20 meters.

• Allowing a 30-meter exchange zone would disrupt the uniformity and timing required in professional relay events.

• Main Theme:

• The baton exchange zone is a crucial component of relay races, ensuring an even playing field and smooth transitions between runners.

• Proper adherence to the 20-meter exchange zone rule is essential for teams to avoid disqualification and maintain competitive performance.

q:
Consider the statements about pawn promotion in chess:

1) A pawn can promote to any piece except king or pawn on reaching the other side.

2) Pawns can only promote to previously captured pieces. Which of the statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points

• Pawn promotion in chess allows a pawn to be exchanged for any piece except the king or another pawn when it reaches the eighth rank.

• The promoted piece can be a queen, rook, bishop, or knight, based on the player's strategic choice.

• Most players choose to promote to a queen due to its powerful capabilities, making it the most common promotion.

• Pawn promotion is a rule that applies universally to all chess games and is not limited by previously captured pieces.

• This rule is designed to increase the dynamics and possibilities in the endgame phase of chess.

Additional Information

• Option 2: The statement that pawns can only promote to previously captured pieces is incorrect.

• Pawn promotion is not restricted by the availability of captured pieces in chess.

• Even if no pieces have been captured, the pawn can still promote to any eligible piece (queen, rook, bishop, or knight).

• This misconception may arise from older variants of the game or misunderstandings of modern chess rules.

• Option 3: The statement that both 1 and 2 are correct is incorrect.

• While Statement 1 is correct, Statement 2 is false, making this option invalid.

• Option 4: The statement that neither 1 nor 2 are correct is incorrect.

• Statement 1 is accurate, meaning this option cannot be correct as it denies the validity of Statement 1.

• Pawn Promotion in Chess:

• Pawn promotion occurs when a pawn reaches the opposite end of the chessboard (the eighth rank for white pawns and the first rank for black pawns).

• The choice of promoted piece can significantly alter the game's dynamics, often shifting the balance of power.

• Promoting to a queen is the most common choice, but players may choose other pieces like knights to create specific tactical opportunities.

• Pawn promotion is a critical strategic element in chess and is often a decisive factor in endgame play.

q: How did Sushil Kumar secure India's first Olympic wrestling medal in 56 years?
options: By winning all his bouts consecutively without any loss
By winning three repechage bouts after losing his opening match
By defeating the reigning champion in the finals
By receiving a walkover in the semifinals
solution:
The correct answer is By winning three repechage bouts after losing his opening match.

Key Points

• Sushil Kumar won the bronze medal in the 66 kg freestyle wrestling category at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

• After losing his opening match to Andriy Stadnik of Ukraine, he entered the repechage round due to Stadnik advancing to the final.

• In the repechage round, Sushil Kumar secured victories in three consecutive bouts against Doug Schwab (USA), Albert Batyrov (Belarus), and Leonid Spiridonov (Kazakhstan).

• He defeated Leonid Spiridonov in the bronze medal match, making history as the first Indian wrestler to win an Olympic medal since Khashaba Dadasaheb Jadhav’s bronze in 1952.

• This achievement brought wrestling back into the spotlight in India and inspired a new generation of wrestlers.

Additional Information

• Option 1: By winning all his bouts consecutively without any loss

• This option is incorrect as Sushil Kumar lost his opening match against Andriy Stadnik. He did not have an undefeated run in the tournament.

• Winning all bouts consecutively is a rare occurrence in wrestling, especially at the Olympic level, due to tough competition.

• Option 3: By defeating the reigning champion in the finals

• This option is incorrect because Sushil Kumar did not compete in the final match of the tournament; he competed in the bronze medal bout.

• He faced Leonid Spiridonov in the repechage round for the bronze medal and not the reigning champion in the finals.

• Option 4: By receiving a walkover in the semifinals

• This option is incorrect as Sushil Kumar did not participate in the semifinals. He advanced through the repechage round after losing his first match.

• In Olympic wrestling, a walkover occurs when an opponent is unable to compete due to injury or other reasons, but this scenario did not apply to Sushil Kumar in the 2008 Olympics.

• Main Theme: Repechage System in Wrestling

• The repechage system gives wrestlers who lose to a finalist a second chance to compete for a bronze medal.

• This system ensures that wrestlers who face strong opponents early in the tournament still have a fair chance at securing a medal.

• It is commonly used in wrestling tournaments, including the Olympics, to maintain competitive fairness.

q: What is the primary focus of Peter Frankopan's book The Silk Roads: A New History of the World?
options: The colonization of the Americas by European powers
The trade disputes between ancient Rome and China
A global history centered on cultural and political exchanges along the Silk Road regions
The history of Western Europe from the Renaissance to the Industrial Revolution
solution:
The correct answer is A global history centered on cultural and political exchanges along the Silk Road regions.

Key Points

• Peter Frankopan's book, "The Silk Roads: A New History of the World," focuses on the interconnectedness of civilizations through cultural, political, and economic exchanges along the Silk Road regions.

• It emphasizes the importance of the Silk Roads as a central axis in the development of global history, challenging the traditional Eurocentric narrative.

• The book highlights how trade routes facilitated the spread of religions, technologies, goods, and ideas across Europe, Asia, and Africa, reshaping the world.

• Frankopan explores historical events and their impact on modern globalization, demonstrating how the Silk Roads have shaped geopolitics over centuries.

• The work provides a comprehensive view of the interactions among diverse cultures, kingdoms, and empires, making it a pivotal contribution to understanding world history.

Additional Information

• Option 1: The colonization of the Americas by European powers

• This topic primarily focuses on the exploration, conquest, and colonization of the Americas by European nations such as Spain, Portugal, France, and Britain between the 15th and 18th centuries.

• It involves the exploitation of indigenous peoples, the transatlantic slave trade, and the establishment of colonial economies based on agriculture, mining, and trade.

• While significant in shaping modern history, this subject is distinct from the Silk Roads' focus on Eurasian interconnectivity.

• Option 2: The trade disputes between ancient Rome and China

• Trade disputes between Rome and China are not a central theme in Frankopan's book.

• Historical interactions between Rome and China were limited, mainly through intermediaries like the Parthians, and focused on goods such as silk and spices.

• The book examines broader patterns of cultural and political exchange rather than specific bilateral trade disputes.

• Option 4: The history of Western Europe from the Renaissance to the Industrial Revolution

• This option pertains to the transformation of Western Europe during the Renaissance (14th–17th centuries) and the subsequent Industrial Revolution (18th–19th centuries).

• While important, this period is Eurocentric and does not capture the global scope of Frankopan's work, which centers on the Silk Roads as a worldwide phenomenon.

• Main Theme: The Silk Roads

• The Silk Roads were ancient trade routes connecting East Asia, Central Asia, the Middle East, and Europe, facilitating the exchange of goods, ideas, and culture.

• They played a crucial role in shaping civilizations, fostering trade networks, and driving cultural diffusion across continents.

q: According to the Global Firepower (GFP) methodology, what is the purpose of using special modifiers like bonuses and penalties in its ranking formula?
options: To exclude non-military nations from the ranking
To prioritize countries with higher nuclear stockpiles
To balance rankings between technologically advanced and lesser-developed nations
To calculate the GDP-to-defense budget ratio
solution:
The correct answer is To balance rankings between technologically advanced and lesser-developed nations.

Key Points

• The Global Firepower (GFP) methodology employs special modifiers, such as bonuses and penalties, to create a balanced and equitable military strength ranking.

• These modifiers ensure that rankings are not overly influenced by a single factor, such as the size of a country's military or its financial resources.

• The goal is to provide a fair comparison between technologically advanced nations with smaller militaries and nations with larger but less technologically advanced forces.

• Modifiers account for variables such as logistical capabilities, geographical factors, and natural resource availability, which play a significant role in a nation's military effectiveness.

• This balanced approach enables the GFP ranking to reflect a more comprehensive view of a nation's overall military strength rather than focusing solely on quantitative metrics.

Additional Information

• Option 1: To exclude non-military nations from the ranking

• While the GFP methodology focuses on military power, it does not specifically aim to exclude non-military nations.

• Instead, it evaluates nations with significant military capabilities and resources, ensuring that all eligible nations are included in the rankings.

• Non-military nations are naturally not part of the GFP ranking as they lack the necessary data points for evaluation.

• Option 2: To prioritize countries with higher nuclear stockpiles

• The GFP ranking does consider nuclear stockpiles as a factor; however, it does not prioritize them disproportionately.

• Nuclear capability is one of many aspects of military power, but it is balanced with other factors like conventional forces, logistics, and economic strength.

• This ensures that nations with smaller nuclear arsenals but strong conventional forces are not unfairly ranked lower.

• Option 4: To calculate the GDP-to-defense budget ratio

• The GDP-to-defense budget ratio is an important economic indicator, but it is not the primary focus of the GFP ranking methodology.

• Instead, the GFP uses a more comprehensive formula that accounts for military, economic, and logistical factors to rank nations.

• While economic strength is a factor, the ranking does not rely solely on financial metrics like GDP ratios.

• Main Theme: Global Firepower (GFP) Ranking

• The GFP ranking is an annual assessment of military strength for nations worldwide, based on over 60 individual factors.

• These factors include manpower, equipment, financial resources, logistical capabilities, and geography.

• The aim is to provide a realistic and balanced comparison of military power across nations, avoiding biases toward specific metrics like sheer size or spending.

• The GFP index uses a "Power Index" score, where lower scores indicate stronger military capabilities.

q: Which of the following statements about basketball equipment specifications is accurate?
options: The backboard must be 1.05 meters wide and 1.80 meters tall.
The diameter of the ring must be exactly 450 mm.
The lines on the backboard must be white and 50 mm wide.
The net must be black with 10 loops to attach it to the ring.
solution:
The correct answer is The lines on the backboard must be white and 50 mm wide.

Key Points

• According to the official basketball equipment specifications set by the International Basketball Federation (FIBA), the lines on the backboard must be white and 50 mm wide.

• The backboard markings include a rectangle above the basketball hoop, which helps players aim and measure their shots accurately.

• These specifications ensure uniformity across basketball courts worldwide, maintaining consistency for professional and amateur games.

• Such precise measurements for the lines are critical for adhering to international standards and ensuring fair play.

• The color white is chosen for the lines for maximum visibility against the standard backboard material, which is often transparent or dark-colored.

Additional Information

• Option 1: The backboard must be 1.05 meters wide and 1.80 meters tall.

• This statement is incorrect. As per FIBA regulations, the standard dimensions of the backboard are 1.80 meters wide and 1.05 meters tall, but the phrasing in the option reverses the dimensions.

• The backboard's dimensions are standardized to ensure uniformity in gameplay across courts globally.

• The backboard is typically made of a transparent material like tempered glass to allow visibility for spectators and players.

• Option 2: The diameter of the ring must be exactly 450 mm.

• This statement is incorrect. The official diameter of the basketball hoop (ring) is 450 mm to 459 mm, as per FIBA standards.

• The inner edge of the ring must have this precise measurement to ensure compatibility with the standard basketball size (No. 7 for men and No. 6 for women).

• The ring is made of steel and must be securely attached to the backboard to withstand the force of dunks and other game actions.

• Option 4: The net must be black with 10 loops to attach it to the ring.

• This statement is incorrect. The net used in basketball is typically made of white cord, not black, for better visibility during gameplay.

• The net is attached to the ring using 12 loops, not 10, ensuring it hangs evenly around the hoop.

• The net's primary function is to slow the ball down after a successful basket, making it easier to identify a score.

• Main Theme: Basketball Equipment Specifications

• Basketball equipment, including the backboard, hoop, net, and court lines, must adhere to precise specifications set by governing bodies like FIBA and the NBA.

• These regulations ensure consistency and fairness in the game, regardless of where it is played.

• Key elements like the dimensions of the backboard, the diameter of the hoop, and the visibility of court markings are all standardized for professional and amateur play.

• The height of the goal post is exactly 2.44 meters (8 feet) from the ground to the underside of the crossbar.

• The width of the goal is 7.32 meters (24 feet), measured between the inside edges of the vertical goalposts.

• The dimensions of the goal post are standardized for all levels of professional football, as per FIFA regulations.

• The goalposts and crossbar must be made of suitable material, typically metal or other approved materials, and must have a consistent shape, often circular or elliptical.

• The goal dimensions are outlined in Law 1 of the Laws of the Game, which governs the field of play.

• The goalpost’s height and width are consistent across all international matches, tournaments, and competitions to ensure uniformity.

• The area around the goal is marked by the goal area and the penalty area, which are also regulated by the Laws of the Game.

• Material and Safety Standards:

• Goalposts are required to be firmly anchored and must not pose any hazard to players.

• They are typically painted white, ensuring visibility during matches and in different lighting conditions.

• Historical Context:

q: Elite long jumpers typically use how many strides in their approach run?
solution:
The correct answer is 18-22.

Key Points

• Elite long jumpers typically take around 18 to 22 strides during their approach run. The number of strides varies depending on the athlete's height, speed, and technique.

• The approach run is a critical phase in the long jump, as it provides the necessary speed and momentum required for an optimal jump.

• Long jumpers aim to achieve their maximum controlled speed during the approach to ensure a powerful take-off at the board.

• The number of strides is carefully determined and practiced to ensure that the jumper can accurately hit the take-off board without overstepping or fouling.

• While 18-22 strides is the typical range, the exact number of strides may vary based on the athlete's training, biomechanics, and personal preferences.

Additional Information

• Phases of Long Jump:

• The long jump consists of four main phases: approach run, take-off, flight, and landing.

• The approach run generates the momentum needed for a successful jump.

• The take-off involves converting horizontal speed into vertical lift.

• The flight phase requires the jumper to maintain balance and maximize the forward motion.

• The landing phase focuses on extending the body forward to maximize the distance covered.

• Importance of Approach Run:

• The approach run is the most important phase in the long jump as it determines the jumper's speed, rhythm, and accuracy.

• Successful long jumpers practice their approach runs extensively to ensure consistency in hitting the take-off board.

• The optimum speed during the approach ensures a balance between horizontal distance and vertical height during the jump.

• Factors Affecting Number of Strides:

• Athlete's height: Taller athletes might require fewer strides due to their longer stride length.

• Strength and speed: Faster and stronger athletes can achieve the desired velocity with fewer strides.

• Experience and technique: Experienced jumpers optimize their stride patterns to hit the take-off board consistently.

• Examples of Elite Long Jumpers:

• Famous long jumpers like Mike Powell and Carl Lewis utilized efficient approach runs with approximately 20 strides to achieve their record-breaking jumps.

• Mike Powell's world record jump of 8.95 meters in 1991 is considered a benchmark in long jump history.

Important Points

• Training for Approach Run:

• Long jumpers focus on improving their sprinting ability, stride length, and take-off accuracy during training.

• Drills like bounding, sprint starts, and plyometric exercises are commonly used to enhance approach run efficiency.

• Regular video analysis helps athletes refine their stride patterns and maintain consistency.

• Key Metrics:

• The average approach run speed for elite male long jumpers is approximately 10.5 m/s, while for female athletes, it is around 9.5 m/s.

• The take-off angle is typically between 18-22 degrees for optimal performance.

• Rules for Long Jump:

• A valid jump requires the athlete to take off from the take-off board without overstepping its edge.

• The jump distance is measured from the edge of the take-off board nearest to the landing pit to the nearest mark made in the sand by any part of the athlete's body.

• Wind assistance must not exceed 2 m/s for a record to be valid.

• The concept of Swaraj was central to the Indian freedom struggle, symbolizing self-rule, self-reliance, and freedom from British dominance.

q: Which of the following is considered a fault in badminton?
options: Shuttle hits net and lands in service box
Server steps on boundary line while serving
Receiver returns the shuttle over the net
solution:
The correct answer is Server steps on boundary line while serving.

Key Points

• Fault in Badminton: A player commits a fault if they step on or over the service boundary line while serving. According to the Badminton World Federation (BWF) rules, the server must stand inside the service court without stepping on the lines when delivering the serve. *This makes Option 2 correct.*

• Shuttle hits net but lands in service box: If the shuttle hits the net during service but still lands within the correct service box, it is considered a legal serve and play continues. *Hence, Option 1 is incorrect.*

• Shuttle lands inside opponent's court: When the shuttle lands inside the opponent's court during play, it is a valid point for the player hitting the shuttle. *Hence, Option 3 is incorrect.*

• Receiver returns the shuttle over the net: Returning the shuttle over the net is a normal action in the game of badminton. It is not considered a fault. *Hence, Option 4 is incorrect.*

• No other options provided beyond Option 4, so Option 5 is not applicable.

Additional Information

• Service Rules in Badminton:

• Both the server and the receiver must stand inside their respective service courts until the serve is made.

• The shuttle must be hit below the server’s waist level, and the racket shaft must point downward during the serve.

• The server's feet must remain stationary and not touch the boundary lines of the service box.

• The shuttlecock must travel diagonally across the net and land within the opponent's service box.

• Common Faults in Badminton:

• Hitting the shuttle outside the court boundaries.

• Shuttle failing to cross the net during play or serve.

• Touching the net with the racket or any part of the body.

• Double hits, where the shuttle is hit twice in succession by the same player.

• Dimensions of a Badminton Court:

• The full length of a standard badminton court is 13.4 meters (44 feet).

• The width is 6.1 meters (20 feet) for doubles and 5.18 meters (17 feet) for singles matches.

• The service courts are divided by a center line, with a short service line and a long service line defining the front and back boundaries.

• Badminton World Federation (BWF) Regulations:

• The BWF is the international governing body for the sport of badminton.

• Its rules and regulations are followed globally in official tournaments and matches.

• Faults, scoring, and other technicalities are clearly defined under the BWF’s Laws of Badminton.

Important Points

• Fault during Service:

• Stepping on the boundary line while serving is a clear violation of the rules and is considered a fault.

• This ensures fair play and prevents the server from gaining an undue advantage by stepping closer to the net.

• Net Faults:

• Touching the net with the racket, body, or clothing during play is also a fault.

• Players must avoid obstructing their opponent’s play by crossing over or under the net.

• Scoring System:

• Badminton matches are played in a best-of-three games format, with each game played to 21 points.

• The winner of a rally scores a point, and the first player or pair to reach 21 points wins the game, provided there is at least a 2-point lead.

q: Which of the following statements about Verghese Kurien is correct?
options: He initiated the White Revolution in India's IT sector.
He pioneered Operation Flood to transform dairy farming.
He invented the milk pasteurization method used in Amul.
He was the first Chairman of the Indian Dairy Association.
solution:
The correct answer is He pioneered Operation Flood to transform dairy farming..

Key Points

• Verghese Kurien is famously known as the Father of the White Revolution in India. His contributions revolutionized the dairy industry, making India the largest producer of milk in the world.

• He spearheaded Operation Flood, launched in 1970, which was one of the largest agricultural movements in the world aimed at increasing milk production and establishing a nationwide milk grid.

• Under Operation Flood, Kurien helped establish the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), which played a pivotal role in ensuring the efficient management of milk production and distribution.

• Amul, the cooperative dairy company, became the face of this revolution. Kurien was instrumental in transforming it into a global success story, using innovative marketing and technology.

• His efforts helped millions of farmers, especially in rural India, gain sustainable livelihoods and improve their socio-economic conditions.

Additional Information

• Operation Flood:

• Launched by the National Dairy Development Board in 1970, the program was funded by the sales of donated powdered milk and butter oil from the European Economic Community.

• The aim was to create a nationwide milk grid to reduce dependence on imports and increase rural income.

• Operation Flood was implemented in three phases, leading to India becoming the largest producer of milk by the 1990s.

• Amul's Role:

• Amul was established in 1946 in Gujarat and became the model for dairy cooperatives across the country.

• Kurien's innovative marketing strategies, such as the iconic "Amul Girl" advertising campaign, helped establish Amul as a household name.

• Amul's success demonstrated the power of cooperative models in empowering farmers.

• White Revolution:

• The White Revolution, led by Kurien, transformed India from a milk-deficient country to the largest producer of milk and dairy products.

• It significantly contributed to improving the nutritional standards of the country.

• The revolution also showcased how agriculture-based industries can drive economic growth.

• Verghese Kurien's Legacy:

• Kurien received numerous accolades, including the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 1963 and the Padma Vibhushan in 1999.

• He served as the Chairman of the NDDB and Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF).

• His autobiography, "I Too Had a Dream", highlights his journey and vision for India's dairy industry.

Important Points

• Incorrect Statement 1: Verghese Kurien did not initiate the White Revolution in India's IT sector; it was focused on dairy farming.

• Incorrect Statement 3: Kurien did not invent the milk pasteurization method used in Amul; pasteurization is a globally recognized process.

• Incorrect Statement 4: He was not the first Chairman of the Indian Dairy Association; his primary contributions were towards NDDB and Amul.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

Key Points

• Statement 1: The book *Negotiating Mughal Law* by Nandini Chatterjee explores legal pluralism and property rights through the experiences of a landlord family across Indian empires. This statement is correct as the book delves into how individuals and families engaged with the Mughal legal system to secure property and navigate rights within the broader context of pre-modern Indian empires.

• Statement 2: The book is described as a literary biography focusing on Mughal emperors' personal lives and poetic patronage. This statement is incorrect. *Negotiating Mughal Law* does not focus on the personal lives or poetic contributions of Mughal emperors but rather examines the legal frameworks and societal dynamics under Mughal rule.

• The book is recognized as a significant contribution to understanding the Mughal legal system and its interaction with individuals, families, and communities.

• The focus of the book is on practical legal negotiations rather than the cultural or artistic patronage of the Mughal emperors.

• Hence, the correct answer is Option 1: Only Statement 1 is correct.

Additional Information

• Legal Pluralism: The term refers to the coexistence of multiple legal systems within a single jurisdiction. In the Mughal Empire, the legal framework included Islamic law (Sharia), customary practices, and local administrative rules.

• Mughal Legal System: The Mughal legal system was deeply rooted in Islamic jurisprudence but also accommodated local traditions and customs to govern a diverse empire.

• Property Rights: Under Mughal rule, property rights were often negotiated through legal documents such as *farmans* (royal decrees) and *sanads* (certificates). Families sought to secure these rights through litigation or petitions.

• Nandini Chatterjee: She is an esteemed historian specializing in legal history and the study of Mughal and colonial India. Her work often explores the intersection of law, society, and culture.

• The book offers valuable insights into the functioning of legal institutions in Mughal India, showing how ordinary individuals and families shaped and were shaped by the law.

Important Points

• Historical Context: The Mughal Empire (1526–1857) governed vast territories in India with a complex administrative and legal system that blended Islamic and indigenous practices.

• Significance of Legal Documents: Legal documents such as court orders, royal decrees, and contracts were essential tools for navigating property disputes and consolidating familial wealth.

• Research Methodology: Nandini Chatterjee employs archival research to reconstruct the narratives of families engaging with Mughal law, providing a unique lens into history.

• Comparative Analysis: The study of Mughal legal practices contributes to understanding broader themes of governance, legal pluralism, and societal dynamics in pre-modern empires.

q: Dr. Tessy Thomas is also known as the 'Missile Woman of India'. She is best associated with which of the following achievements?
options: Led Agni-V project; began career at LRDE
solution:
The correct answer is Led Agni-V project; began career at LRDE.

Key Points

• Dr. Tessy Thomas is popularly referred to as the 'Missile Woman of India' due to her significant contributions to India's missile development programs, particularly the Agni series of missiles.
• She played a pivotal role in leading the Agni-V project, one of India's most advanced intercontinental ballistic missiles (ICBMs) with a range of over 5,000 km. This missile added strategic deterrence capabilities to India's defense arsenal.
• Dr. Tessy began her career at the Electronics and Radar Development Establishment (LRDE), a lab of the Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO), where she worked on the design and development of various radar systems.
• She has been associated with the DRDO for over three decades, specializing in missile guidance, control, and system integration. Her expertise and leadership have earned her national and international recognition.
• Dr. Tessy Thomas is the first woman to head a missile project in India, breaking stereotypes and inspiring women across the country to pursue careers in science and technology.
Additional Information

• Agni-V Missile:
• The Agni-V missile is an advanced nuclear-capable intercontinental ballistic missile developed by India under the Integrated Guided Missile Development Program (IGMDP).
• It has a range of 5,000 to 8,000 km, making it capable of striking targets far beyond India's immediate neighborhood, including regions in Asia, Europe, and Africa.
• The missile features a three-stage solid propulsion system and advanced technologies for precision targeting and survivability.
• The successful development of Agni-V enhances India's strategic deterrence capabilities and positions the country as a global power in missile technology.
• The project represents India's commitment to maintaining a credible minimum deterrent and strengthening its national security.

• Her academic excellence and passion for research led her to join the DRDO, where she contributed significantly to India's defense sector.
• Role in DRDO:
• Dr. Tessy Thomas joined the DRDO in 1988 and has been instrumental in the design, development, and deployment of strategic missile systems.
• She has worked on several projects, including the Agni-I, Agni-II, Agni-III, and Agni-IV missiles, before leading the Agni-V program.

q: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the author and thematic focus of the novel "A Fine Balance"?
options: Salman Rushdie, focusing on post-colonial identity and magical realism
Rohinton Mistry, exploring social injustices during India's Emergency period
Jhumpa Lahiri, depicting the immigrant experience in 1980s New York
Arundhati Roy, examining environmental activism and political corruption
solution:
The correct answer is Rohinton Mistry, exploring social injustices during India's Emergency period.

Key Points

• "A Fine Balance" is a novel written by Rohinton Mistry, a celebrated Indian-Canadian author, published in 1995.

• The novel is set during the tumultuous period of India's Emergency (1975-1977), declared by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.

• The book primarily focuses on the themes of social injustice, caste discrimination, and the struggles of marginalized communities in India.

• The story revolves around four characters from diverse backgrounds who come together during the Emergency, exploring their lives amidst political upheaval and personal hardships.

• "A Fine Balance" has received widespread acclaim for its rich character development, poignant storytelling, and vivid depiction of the socio-political realities of India.

Additional Information

• About Rohinton Mistry:

• Rohinton Mistry was born in 1952 in Bombay (Mumbai), India, and later immigrated to Canada in the late 1970s.

• He is known for his works that explore the socio-political landscapes of India, including novels like "Such a Long Journey" and "Family Matters".

• Rohinton Mistry is a recipient of numerous awards, including the Commonwealth Writers' Prize and nominations for the Booker Prize.

• The Emergency Period in India:

• The Emergency lasted from 1975 to 1977 and was declared by Indira Gandhi, citing internal disturbances.

• During this period, fundamental rights were suspended, press censorship was imposed, and political opponents were jailed.

• The Emergency is widely regarded as one of the darkest chapters in Indian democracy, with significant socio-political impacts.

• Other Works Exploring India's Emergency:

• Books like "Midnight's Children" by Salman Rushdie also explore the socio-political changes during India's post-independence era, including the Emergency.

• Documentaries and films such as "Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi" have depicted the impact of the Emergency on India’s youth and society.

• Significance of "A Fine Balance":

• The novel is regarded as a masterpiece in contemporary literature, shedding light on the human cost of political decisions.

• It has been included in several academic curriculums and remains a favorite among literary critics and readers.

Important Points

• Option Analysis:

• Salman Rushdie: Known for works like "Midnight's Children," which focus on post-colonial identity and magical realism, but he did not write "A Fine Balance." *Incorrect*.

• Rohinton Mistry: The author of "A Fine Balance," focusing on social injustices during India's Emergency period. *Correct*.

• Jhumpa Lahiri: Famous for works like "The Namesake", which explore the immigrant experience, but this is unrelated to "A Fine Balance." *Incorrect*.

• Arundhati Roy: Known for works like "The God of Small Things", which examine environmental activism and political corruption, but she did not write "A Fine Balance." *Incorrect*.

q: Which American author received the Pulitzer Prize for "Beloved" and was later awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993?
solution:
The correct answer is Toni Morrison.

Key Points

• Toni Morrison is a renowned American author who received the Pulitzer Prize in 1988 for her novel *Beloved*. The book is considered one of her masterpieces, exploring themes of slavery, motherhood, and memory.
• She was awarded the prestigious Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993, becoming the first African-American woman to achieve this honor. The Nobel Committee recognized her for her visionary force and the poetic nature of her work.
• *Beloved*, published in 1987, is a critically acclaimed novel that tells the haunting story of a woman named Sethe, a former slave, who is haunted by the ghost of her deceased child. The novel is based on real historical events and explores the psychological scars of slavery.
• Toni Morrison’s works often focus on African-American experiences, history, and identity, with a strong emphasis on the struggles and resilience of Black women.
• In addition to *Beloved*, Morrison authored several other impactful novels, including *Sula*, *The Bluest Eye*, *Song of Solomon*, and *Jazz*, all of which have cemented her legacy as one of the most influential writers in American literature.
Additional Information

• Toni Morrison’s Early Life:
• Toni Morrison was born as Chloe Anthony Wofford on February 18, 1931, in Lorain, Ohio, USA.
• She attended Howard University and Cornell University, where she studied English, and later became an editor at Random House, promoting African-American authors.
• The Pulitzer Prize:
• The Pulitzer Prize is an annual award for achievements in newspaper, magazine, online journalism, literature, and musical composition in the United States.
• Toni Morrison received this award for *Beloved* in 1988, which further solidified her reputation as a literary giant.
• The Nobel Prize in Literature:
• Toni Morrison was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1993, with the committee praising her for novels characterized by visionary force and poetic import.
• This recognition marked an important milestone for African-American literature on the global stage.
• Other Prominent Works:
• *The Bluest Eye* (1970): A novel about a young African-American girl who yearns for blue eyes and struggles with societal beauty standards.
• *Song of Solomon* (1977): A richly textured novel about African-American culture, history, and identity, which won the National Book Critics Circle Award.
• *Sula* (1973): A story of friendship and betrayal set in a Black community in Ohio.
• Legacy:
• Toni Morrison passed away on August 5, 2019, at the age of 88, leaving behind a profound legacy in literature and a lasting impact on readers worldwide.
• Her works continue to be studied in academic institutions and cherished by readers for their deep exploration of race, identity, and humanity.
Important Points

• Other Options Explained:
• Alice Walker: Best known for her novel *The Color Purple*, which won the Pulitzer Prize for Fiction in 1983. She did not win the Nobel Prize.
• Maya Angelou: Celebrated poet and author, known for her autobiographical series beginning with *I Know Why the Caged Bird Sings*. She was not a Nobel laureate.
• Zora Neale Hurston: Known for her novel *Their Eyes Were Watching God*, she was a prominent figure in the Harlem Renaissance but did not receive the Pulitzer or Nobel Prize.
